subject: mathematics_1b
question_text: Prove that the product of the perpendicular distances from the origin to the pair of straight lines represented by ax²+2hxy+by²+2gx+2fy+c=0 is |c| / √((a−b)²+4h²).

mark_split.label: Split the pair and match coefficients
Convert to a, h, b and c

recall_prompt: Say how you would prove this — say what the distance from the ORIGIN simplifies to, and what the numerator becomes.

steps.label: Split the pair and match coefficients
steps.margin_note: First mark. A general pair splits into two general lines, each carrying its own constant — and those constants are what the perpendicular distances from the origin will use.
lines: Let the separate equations of ax² + 2hxy + by² + 2gx + 2fy + c = 0 be
l₁x + m₁y + n₁ = 0  ……(1)  and  l₂x + m₂y + n₂ = 0  ……(2)
∴ ax² + 2hxy + by² + 2gx + 2fy + c ≡ (l₁x + m₁y + n₁)(l₂x + m₂y + n₂)
Comparing both sides we get  l₁l₂ = a,  m₁m₂ = b,  n₁n₂ = c,

recall.must_convey: That the pair splits into two general lines and the coefficients are matched, including n₁n₂ = c.
accept: split into two general lines and match the coefficients
l one l two is a, m one m two is b and n one n two is c
the constants multiply to give c
rendu lines ga split chesi coefficients match cheyyali
n one n two equals c is the one that matters here
heard_as: n one n two equals c

steps.why: n₁n₂ = c is the key entry: the perpendicular from the ORIGIN to a line is just its constant over the root, so the product of the two perpendiculars will carry n₁n₂ — which is c.
common_mistakes: Forgetting that the constants also have to be matched.
Pairing the cross terms with the same subscript.
steps.memory_tip: A general pair splits into two lines each with its OWN constant — those constants do the work.

steps.label: Write both perpendicular distances
steps.margin_note: One mark. From the ORIGIN the distance formula collapses: putting (0,0) into |l x + m y + n| leaves only |n|. Both numerators are therefore single constants.
lines: The perpendicular distance from O(0,0) to line (1) is  p₁ = |n₁| / √(l₁² + m₁²)
The perpendicular distance from O(0,0) to line (2) is  p₂ = |n₂| / √(l₂² + m₂²)

recall.must_convey: That from the origin each perpendicular distance is |n|/√(l² + m²).
accept: from the origin the distance is just mod n over the root
putting zero zero into the formula leaves only the constant
p one is mod n one over root l one squared plus m one squared
origin nunchi distance ante n matrame
both distances from the origin

steps.why: This is what makes the origin version SHORTER than the general-point version: the numerator has one term instead of two.
common_mistakes: Carrying α and β through when the point is the origin.
steps.memory_tip: From the ORIGIN the formula collapses: putting (0,0) in leaves only |n|.

steps.label: Multiply them together
steps.margin_note: One mark. Multiply the two fractions. The numerator is immediately n₁n₂, which the matched coefficients already give; only the denominator needs work.
lines: ∴ The product of the perpendiculars is

recall.must_convey: That multiplying gives |n₁n₂| = |c| over the expanded product of the two roots.
accept: multiply the two distances so the numerator becomes n one n two which is c
the numerator is mod c straight away
expand the product under the root

steps.why: The numerator finishes in one step because c was matched directly — all the remaining work is in the denominator, exactly as in the general-point version.
common_mistakes: Adding rather than multiplying the two distances.
Forgetting to multiply the two roots under one square root.
steps.memory_tip: The numerator is n₁n₂ straight away; only the denominator needs work.

steps.label: Convert to a, h, b and c
steps.margin_note: The last mark. Add and subtract 2l₁l₂m₁m₂ under the root so it regroups as a difference of squares plus a square — the same rearrangement the general-point version uses.

recall.must_convey: That the denominator regroups as (a − b)² + (2h)², giving |c|/√((a − b)² + 4h²).
accept: add and subtract the same term so the denominator regroups
it becomes a minus b squared plus four h squared
substitute the matched coefficients into the denominator
denominator ni a minus b square plus four h square ga rayali
this gives the required result

steps.why: The added and subtracted terms cancel exactly, and (l₁m₂ + l₂m₁)² is (2h)² = 4h² — which is where the 4 in the answer comes from.
steps.memory_tip: Add and subtract 2l₁l₂m₁m₂ under the root so it regroups into a difference of squares plus a square.

insider_note: The constants have to be matched as well: n₁n₂ = c is what makes the numerator collapse to |c|. The denominator is the same (a − b)² + 4h² as the (α, β) version, so the two proofs differ only at the top.
